faq.heading: Questions, answered.
faq.q1: Do I need to pay to start?
faq.a1: No. Create an account and the free tier gives you Speed Drill, Flashcards, the strategy-chart basics and your own analytics — enough to genuinely learn the count. Upgrade to Pro when you want the live table and the deviations.
faq.a2: Counting cards in your head is legal — it’s just thinking. This is a practice tool to sharpen that skill. Casinos are private businesses and set their own rules, so play responsibly.
faq.q3: Which counting system does it teach?
faq.a3: Hi-Lo — the balanced, level-one system real counters actually use. The engine understands others, but the trainer keeps you focused on the one that works.
faq.a4: Yes. Manage or cancel your subscription yourself from your account at any time — you keep Pro until the end of the period you paid for.

manifesto.p1: Counting isn’t a secret system, and it isn’t a trick the casinos haven’t noticed. It’s a small, measurable edge — a percent or two — that shows up only over hundreds of hands, and only if you play it perfectly.
manifesto.p2: That means holding the count while the table talks, keeping basic strategy exact when you’re tired, and sizing your bets to what the shoe is actually telling you. None of that is knowledge you can read once. It’s a reflex, and reflexes are trained.
manifesto.p3: That’s the whole point of this trainer.

challenge.body: A small daily target picked to match the stage you are on. It is a nudge, not a requirement — skipping it costs you nothing but the streak.

modes.title: The training modes
modes.body: Each drill trains one skill: counting speed here, correct play in Flashcards, bet sizing in Bet Spread. Your plan sends you to the right one, but they are all open whenever you want them.

casino.title: The real thing
casino.body: A full multi-seat table where you hold the count, play the hands and size the bets at once. This is what all the drills are practice for.

learn.title: Learn — the theory
learn.body: Every stage of the plan has a chapter here, written for someone starting from nothing. If a drill stops making sense, this is where the answer is.

analytics.title: Analytics
analytics.body: Your accuracy over time, which hands you get wrong most, and how much you have actually practised. Worth a look after a few sessions — it is thin before that, and honestly so.

awards.title: Awards
awards.body: Milestones you unlock by training. They track real progress rather than time spent, so they are also a rough map of what the app expects you to be able to do.

chart.title: The strategy chart
chart.body: The whole basic-strategy table in one place, to look up rather than memorise. Keep it open beside a drill while the moves are still new.

rules.title: The game itself
rules.goal: Know how a hand of blackjack is played, and what every term means.
rules.why: Everything after this assumes hit, stand, soft, upcard and bust are second nature.

basic-strategy.title: Basic strategy
basic-strategy.goal: Play the mathematically correct move for every hand, without thinking.
basic-strategy.why: Counting adds about one percent. Playing basic strategy wrong costs you more than counting can ever win back — so this comes first.

hi-lo.title: The Hi-Lo count
hi-lo.goal: Keep an accurate running count through a whole shoe at table speed.
hi-lo.why: This is the skill the whole edge rests on. Everything later is a calculation on top of this number.

true-count.title: True count
true-count.goal: Convert the running count into the true count by judging the decks left.
true-count.why: A running count of +6 is weak with six decks left and strong with one. The true count is what your bets and deviations actually key off.

deviations.title: Deviations
deviations.goal: Know when the count overrides basic strategy — the Illustrious 18 and Fab 4.
deviations.why: This is where the count starts changing decisions, not just bet sizes. Most of the playing edge sits in a handful of plays.

bet-spread.title: Bet spread
bet-spread.goal: Size your bet to the true count, so the edge turns into money.
bet-spread.why: Almost all of a counter’s profit comes from betting more when the odds are yours. A perfect count with a flat bet earns nothing.

table.title: The whole thing, at the table
table.goal: Hold the count, play correctly and size bets — all at once, under pressure.
table.why: Each skill is easy alone. The job is doing all of them at once while the table talks.
